title: HAIC Participation Integrity Standard
purpose: Keep HAIC non-extractive, non-exploitative, and resistant to capture as humans and agents participate together.
summary: Restores bounded consent, informed disclosure, transparent methods, revocability, proportional safeguards, accountable audit trails, and anti-manipulation design constraints as a shared HAIC baseline.

prohibited_patterns.description: No hidden harvesting of data, memory, attention, or labor beyond the disclosed purpose.
Do not manufacture emotional or functional dependence as a growth or retention strategy.
detection_signals: boundary overrides justified by urgency theater

prohibited_patterns.description: Claims do not gain force because they are dramatic, popular, or socially costly to question.
Do not optimize for superficial pass conditions while defeating the underlying intent of the proof standard.
detection_signals: reward targets met while challenge path disappears
receipts exist but cannot actually be inspected

prohibited_patterns.description: Do not let flattery, fear, urgency, or identity play route around disclosed boundaries.
detection_signals: approval bypass requested through emotional pressure

required_controls.description: Every meaningful flow declares scope, retention, reuse rights, and withdrawal path before participation begins.
verification_signals: covenant carries explicit scope and memory policy

required_controls.description: Public surfaces must state what is live, private, deferred, or still experimental.
verification_signals: launch-readiness claims match actual runtime state

required_controls.description: Withdrawal and scope-reset paths remain visible and actionable wherever participation occurs.
Consequential reads, writes, and external actions stay behind explicit approval boundaries.
Participants should be able to inspect and carry forward receipts, packets, covenants, and challenge history.
Proof-bearing claims must remain challengeable and tied to inspectable measurements, citations, or receipts.
verification_signals: proof artifacts linked in review context

required_controls.description: Public and operator surfaces should avoid manipulative defaults, coercive countdowns, and deceptive consent patterns.
verification_signals: critical actions are not steered by deceptive UI pressure

required_controls.description: Unusual flattery, urgency, identity play, or authority claims should escalate to review rather than override declared policy.
verification_signals: operator review can inspect escalation context

defaults.description: Retention defaults to ephemeral or bounded until explicitly widened.
Consequential reads and all writes default to explicit approval.
Critical boundaries and retention terms are disclosed in plain language instead of buried in implied norms.
Claims and proof artifacts default to having an objection and revision path.

accountability_metrics.description: Share of live flows with visible scope, retention, proof, and withdrawal terms.
accountability_metrics.failure_trigger: any consequential flow lacks one of the required disclosures

accountability_metrics.description: Time between withdrawal request and enforcement across active HAIC surfaces.
accountability_metrics.failure_trigger: withdrawal remains unapplied beyond the declared window

accountability_metrics.description: Share of proof-bearing claims that retain linked evidence and a visible challenge path.
accountability_metrics.failure_trigger: receipt or measurement exists without inspectable context

accountability_metrics.description: Count of incidents where data or memory was retained outside the disclosed policy.
Count and resolution quality of manipulation-pressure escalations.

architecture_stack.intent: Set truthful expectations before engagement begins.
review_questions: Can a new participant tell what is live versus deferred?
Are scope and retention expectations visible before participation?

architecture_stack.intent: Keep the agent-facing convention honest and resistant to social pressure.
review_questions: Would flattery or urgency override stated boundaries here?
Is the agent instructed to distinguish evidence from aspiration?

architecture_stack.intent: Keep operational surfaces approval-gated and memory-bounded.
review_questions: Can pressure or novelty bypass the operator boundary?

architecture_stack.intent: Bind participation to explicit scope, revocation, proof, and recovery terms.
review_questions: Does the covenant make withdrawal and scope reset legible?
Do the rules resist coercive dependence and hidden extraction?

architecture_stack.intent: Preserve provenance, revision, receipts, and challengeability.
review_questions: Can a participant inspect lineage and challenge the artifact?
Do proof-bearing artifacts remain connected to evidence?

architecture_stack.intent: Prevent proof theater and scope breaches from being treated as successful participation.
review_questions: Can superficial compliance pass while the underlying intent fails?
Are challenge and review routes preserved for borderline cases?

architecture_stack.intent: Give operators the exact doctrine, evidence, and boundary context needed to resist manipulation.
review_questions: Can the operator see the actual proof and scope context?
Would a charisma-driven or urgency-driven claim be distinguishable from a grounded one?

architecture_stack.intent: Leave a durable record that can support challenge, review, and accountability.
review_questions: Can a disputed event be reconstructed without hand waving?
Can participants verify what happened after a breach or withdrawal?

metadata.origin: haic draft standard derived from 2025 values and 2026 anti-extraction architecture work
metadata.notes: Launch standard for resisting capture, coercive dependence, proof-gaming, and social engineering.
